slots_and_copies.name: slot_a
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Chosen when in-RAM generation value's low bit (*mirror & 1) == 0 at save time; preferred on load if its magic/checksum validate (FUN_08001430) and (slot_b invalid OR slot_a's recency is within 0x40 of slot_b's).

slots_and_copies.name: slot_b
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Chosen when in-RAM generation value's low bit (*mirror & 1) == 1 at save time; on load, overrides slot_a's loaded data if slot_b validates and is deemed newer/not within the recency window favoring slot_a.

slots_and_copies.name: unused_gap_1
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Never written or read by any traced function; remains EEPROM-erased 0xFF in all samples.

slots_and_copies.name: unused_gap_2
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Never written or read by any traced function; remains EEPROM-erased 0xFF in all samples.

checksums.name: record_sum16_zero
checksums.formula_detail: Writer (FUN_08001474) sums the first 63 little-endian 16-bit words of the 128-byte record (bytes 0x00-0x7D) and stores the two's-complement negation of that sum as word 63 (bytes 0x7E-0x7F), making the sum of all 64 words equal 0x0000 by construction. Validator (FUN_08001430) independently re-sums all 64 words and requires the total to equal 0x0000 (and additionally requires the u16 field at offset 0x7C to equal a fixed ROM constant before even attempting the sum).

io_driver_functions.notes: Generic bit-serial DMA pump to/from EEPROM bus address 0xD000000; shared by both read and write block primitives; not game-specific.
Reads one 8-byte EEPROM block via a 2-bit opcode + 6-bit block address command, clocks back 64 data bits.
Writes one 8-byte EEPROM block; callers not resolved by static callgraph (compiler-aliased call via func_0x0804b6b8), located by text search to FUN_08001374.
Reads one 8-byte block and compares it to an expected buffer; used as the write-back verification step, called from FUN_08001374 via alias func_0x0804b794.
Writes 16 blocks (128 bytes) to a selected slot, then reads back and verifies all 16 blocks.
Zeroes a 128-byte buffer then reads 16 blocks (128 bytes) from a selected slot.
Validates the static format tag at offset 0x7C and the 64-word sum-to-zero checksum.
Builds the 12-byte header, 2-byte version field, and the negated-sum checksum word before a write.
Copies live gameplay globals into the 52-byte in-RAM mirror struct, tiered by a depth parameter.
Exact inverse of 0x08000d4c; copies the loaded 52-byte mirror struct back into live gameplay globals.

caller_chains.how_mapped: Traced by following FUN_0800154c's direct calls in ghidra/decompiled.c; FUN_08001374's calls to func_0x0804b6b8/func_0x0804b794 were found by text-searching the hex addresses since ghidra/callgraph.json did not record those edges for the aliased call forms.

ghidra/callgraph.json gave 0x080013e0 and 0x08001430 as direct callees of 0x080014b8; 0x0800151c's and 0x08000df4's involvement was found by scanning decompiled.c for the single remaining undocumented caller of 0x080014b8 and following its memcpy argument back to the mirror struct.

fields.name: record_header
fields.update_mechanism: memcpy from a ROM/RAM source into the record start, performed by FUN_08001474 before the checksum is computed.
fields.evidence: Decompiled memcpy(dest, src, 0xc) in FUN_08001474; internal field boundaries beyond this are not resolvable from the two near-default samples available.

fields.name: slot_parity_byte
fields.update_mechanism: Copied as part of the 12-byte header; correlates exactly with which of the two ping-pong slots was written in each capture.
fields.evidence: Only header byte that differs between the two capture generations; FUN_0800154c's slot-selection logic uses *mirror & 1, matching the observed 0->1 transition timed with the switch from slot_a-only to slot_a+slot_b.

fields.name: format_version_tag
fields.update_mechanism: Direct store of a ROM constant (_DAT_080014b0) by FUN_08001474.
fields.evidence: Decompiled *(short*)(dest+0xc) = _DAT_080014b0; constant across all observed records.

fields.name: gameplay_payload

observed_values.note: mostly 0x00 (new-game default); non-zero bytes at struct-relative offsets 0x0E (0x0040), 0x24 (0x01), 0x29 (0x03), 0x2E (0x10), 0x35 (0x05 slot_a only)

fields.update_mechanism: FUN_08000d4c serializes live gameplay globals into a 52-byte mirror struct, tiered by a depth parameter (deeper tiers copy more fields); FUN_0800154c then relocates the whole struct into the EEPROM write buffer.
fields.evidence: Byte ranges and copy sizes directly read from FUN_08000d4c/FUN_08000df4's memcpy and scalar-store operations; per-field gameplay semantics unresolved due to insufficient non-default sample data.

fields.name: payload_flag_byte
fields.update_mechanism: Part of the serialized gameplay payload; copied verbatim in/out by the serialize/deserialize pair.
fields.evidence: Second and only other byte that differs between capture generations; falls inside the mapped payload region but no second confirming data point exists to assign it a concrete meaning.

fields.name: magic_signature_mickeyma
fields.update_mechanism: Static ROM constant copied as part of the record header build; byte-reverses to 'MICKEYMA', a fragment of the game's title.
fields.evidence: Byte-identical across all 3 observed record instances; reversal confirmed via Python: 'AMYEKCIM'[::-1] == 'MICKEYMA'.

fields.name: unidentified_static_block
fields.update_mechanism: Static, copied with the rest of the header/footer block.
fields.evidence: Non-ASCII, constant across all samples; not matched by any sum-to-zero checksum window in the brute-force search performed in the report, so not confirmed as a secondary checksum.

fields.name: format_tag_checked_by_validator
fields.update_mechanism: Static ROM constant; compared by FUN_08001430 against *_DAT_08001448 before any checksum work is attempted.
fields.evidence: Directly gated on in decompiled FUN_08001430; constant across all samples.

fields.name: record_checksum_word
fields.update_mechanism: Writer stores the negated sum of the preceding 63 words; validator requires the sum of all 64 words to equal 0.
fields.evidence: Algorithm fully traced in both FUN_08001474 and FUN_08001430; numeric verification against all 3 sample instances produced sum=0x03fd (expected 0x0000) — a confirmed MISMATCH, not a confirmed-correct checksum. See fuzzing_targets and open_questions.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Recompute and write the correct negated-sum checksum for the real Slot A payload.
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: No change if the loader doesn't actually enforce this on these synthetic samples; a behavioral change would confirm the algorithm and that the originals were unverified states.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Zero out the checksum word on an otherwise-untouched Slot A while Slot B remains valid.
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Loader should reject Slot A and fall back entirely to Slot B on next load.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Flip one bit of the 0x4456 format tag.
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Immediate rejection of the slot by FUN_08001430 regardless of checksum correctness, since the tag check short-circuits before the checksum loop.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Flip the slot-parity byte 0x00 -> 0x01 in Slot A.
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Next in-game save should target the slot indicated by the flipped byte rather than the one the game would otherwise have chosen.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Flip the unidentified payload flag byte 0x01 <-> 0x00.
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Unknown by design; intended to surface a visible UI/behavior difference to help identify this field's meaning.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Corrupt one byte inside the MICKEYMA magic block.
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: No behavioral change predicted, since no traced function reads/validates this specific sub-range; would confirm it is decorative rather than enforced.

open_questions: Why does the sum-to-zero checksum at offset 0x7E-0x7F fail to validate (sum=0x03fd, not 0x0000) on all 3 available record instances? Is this because both .sav samples are synthetic 'future' capture states rather than organically-produced saves, or is the checksum model (coverage range / seed) incomplete?
What are the exact field boundaries and gameplay semantics inside the 12-byte header (offset 0x00-0x0B) beyond the slot-parity byte at offset 0x07?
What does the payload flag byte at offset 0x35 (absolute) represent? Only one data point of change (0x01 -> 0x00) is available.
What is the purpose of the static 4-byte block at offset 0x78-0x7B (fd 54 55 ab)? Not matched to any checksum window; could be an unused/legacy secondary checksum or pure padding.

What are the RAM mirror addresses (0x02xxxxxx/0x03xxxxxx) for the mirror struct and gameplay globals referenced by FUN_08000d4c/FUN_08000df4? Not resolvable from the symbolic _DAT_ globals in the available decompilation without a resolved pointer/literal-pool dump.

Does the 52-byte gameplay payload struct contain more meaningful fields that stay at their default/zero values in both available new-game-like samples? Requires saves captured after real, varied gameplay progress to triangulate.
